instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The Romans left Britain in AD 410 because their empire had become too large and costly to defend. Roman Britain had been unstable for some time due to raids from neighbouring tribes, and now Rome itself was being attacked too. The army was needed closer to home.
atoms.sound: The Romans left Britain in AD four hundred and ten because their empire had become too large and costly to defend. Roman Britain had been unstable for some time due to raids from neighbouring tribes, and now Rome itself was being attacked too. The army was needed closer to home.

atoms.text: When the Romans left, the Britons lost many things, including educated writers. Due to the lack of writing, historians later called this period the “Dark Ages”.

atoms.a: Why did the Romans leave Britain?
b: ++Roman soldiers were needed back home to defend Rome.
The weather in Britain was too cold for Roman soldiers.
They were defeated by the local tribes.

atoms.a: Why is the time after the Romans called the Dark Ages?
b: There were no battles or important events during this time.
++There were few written records from this time.

instruction.text: Without the organisation of the Romans, what might have become harder to make?

feedback.end: Making coins requires lots of time and resources — plus, everyone needs to agree on the currency to use! After the Romans left, the Britons stopped using coins for a couple of centuries.

instruction.text: Sort the farmer’s produce to learn more about trade in the Dark Ages.

feedback.finish: Without coins, Britons used a barter system. This meant that they traded goods based on need. For example, a farmer might trade his grain for a blacksmith’s tools.

hint.label: Magistrate
hint.text: Magistrates were Roman officials in charge of collecting taxes and enforcing laws.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in this conversation between a Roman magistrate and a Briton.

atoms.b: It is time to pay your ((++taxes electricity_bill)). We need money to defend against the raiders.
I don’t see an ((++army writers)). We know that all your soldiers have left! Who exactly are we supposed to be paying for?
Well ... forget about that. We still need money to keep the courts running and uphold the ((++law stone_houses)).
What use are your ((++Roman Briton)) laws if you can’t protect us from the ((++raiding trading)) tribes? The attacks have been going on for ages!
You Britons would fall apart without our rules and ((++organisation togas)).
You’ve got no power here without your ((cooks ++soldiers)). Go back to ((++Rome Scotland)) and leave us be!

feedback.finish: Roman government in Britain broke down very quickly after their army left because the magistrates could no longer enforce any laws.
